research: A major 2019 review links higher dietary-fiber intake with better long-term health outcomes in prospective cohorts; its randomized trials measured risk factors such as cholesterol and blood pressure. These are different evidence types: cohort associations are not randomized proof of reduced deaths. Supplement trials and participants with chronic disease were excluded from this review. A linked correction remains unresolved in our audit, so new quantitative estimates from this review are held pending verification.
context: Fiber grams do not identify the specific fiber, its viscosity, fermentability, dose or food matrix. Evidence about fiber-rich foods cannot automatically be transferred to isolated fibers, and a change in a blood marker or gut microbe is not proof of fewer clinical events. No named fiber is assigned a universal good/bad score in this batch.
psyllium: A 2018 meta-analysis included 28 randomized trials (1,924 participants), lasting at least three weeks, with a median psyllium amount around 10.2 g/day. LDL cholesterol fell by 0.33 mmol/L on average (95% CI 0.27–0.38 lower); evidence certainty for LDL was moderate because results varied across trials. This is a lipid-marker finding, not proof that this product prevents heart attacks or a recommended personal dose. Full text and disclosures remain unaudited.
newer: A 2025 review also reported lower LDL with psyllium but substantial heterogeneity (LDL I-squared about 88%) and a small-study-effect signal. Its risk-of-bias table labels every listed comparison high risk, and several entries are arms from the same trial. Study-count terminology, shared controls and unit reporting need independent verification before its pooled numerical effect is used in the app. It overlaps older evidence and is not independent replication of every trial.
fermentable: A systematic review of inulin-type fructans included 78 publications, not necessarily 78 independent trials, targeting generally healthy adults. Many studies found increased Bifidobacterium, while other microbiota and short-chain-fatty-acid results varied. Microbial abundance changes alone do not establish symptom improvement or a benefit for every person; chain length, dose and baseline diet may matter.
high: Inulin/fructan studies report gas, bloating, cramping and other digestive symptoms in some participants, with responses varying by form, amount and person. These findings do not establish a universal excess-fiber threshold, do not apply identically to psyllium or food fiber, and do not diagnose intolerance from an ingredient name. This batch supplies no personal escalation schedule, treatment advice or product-level safety verdict.
reference: The US Nutrition Facts Daily Value for dietary fiber is 28 g. It is a labeling reference, not a tolerable upper limit, personal requirement or recommended supplement dose. Total fiber grams cannot reveal how much of a particular named fiber is present when a mixture is used.

Fiber.status: Partial research draft; not clinically reviewed; not integrated into UI
Fiber.scope: Reynolds and Jovanovski abstracts; selected Hughes and Gholami review sections; previously verified FDA label reference. This is not an exhaustive current review of all fibers or clinical populations.
Fiber.disclosures: Reynolds lists the Health Research Council of New Zealand, WHO, Riddet Centre of Research Excellence, Healthier Lives National Science Challenge, University of Otago and Otago Southland Diabetes Research Trust as funders; author conflicts and funder roles remain unchecked. Jovanovski project funding/conflicts were not established from the abstract. Hughes and Gholami project-specific funding, author disclosures and sponsor roles were not established in the sections retrieved; absence of extracted information is not no funding or no conflicts.
Fiber.standing: FLAG: PubMed lists a correction to Reynolds 2019 (PMID 30712898; DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(19)30119-9). Attempts to retrieve the notice failed; its substance and impact remain unknown. No retraction is inferred. New quantitative general-fiber claims are held. Independent standing checks for the other sources have not been completed.
Fiber.release_gate: Research record only. Before public education integration, resolve the Reynolds correction or omit reliance on that source, complete source-specific disclosures for the published claims, and test both sheet entry points. Do not publish the newer psyllium pooled estimate until extraction/unit and shared-control questions are resolved.
